title: What is Dispatch?
overview: Dispatch is a Redux function used to send actions to the store. It starts the process of updating application state.

title: How Dispatch Works
overview: When dispatch is called, the action is sent to reducers. Reducers process the action and update the store.

example.title: Dispatch Flow
example.content:
Component
 ↓
Dispatch
 ↓
Action
 ↓
Reducer
 ↓
Store Update

title: Dispatching Actions from Components
overview: React components can trigger Redux state changes by using dispatch with actions.

title: Synchronous Data Flow
overview: Redux normally follows synchronous data flow where actions immediately reach reducers and update the store.

title: Asynchronous Dispatch
overview: Async operations like API calls require middleware such as Redux Thunk to dispatch actions after completing asynchronous tasks.

example.title: Async Flow
example.content:
API Call
 ↓
Thunk
 ↓
Dispatch Success Action
 ↓
Update Store

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how dispatch sends actions, how Redux data flows, and how synchronous and asynchronous updates work.
